name: Misdirected & Lost Shipments
owner: Account owner or team lead for the shipment
trigger: A shipment is delivered to an incorrect address or cannot be recovered in transit.
purpose: A consistent, documented process for shipments sent to the wrong address or lost in transit. It fixes accountability, the recovery steps that must be tried first, and how a credit is decided, so client relationships hold and cost lands on whoever caused the error. Applies to anything Brick orders or orders for a client, including vendor-fulfilled orders such as Uline.
doneWhen: Every recovery step is documented, fault is assigned, and the resolution is issued and communicated in writing.

steps.title: Determine who provided the incorrect address
steps.trigger: A shipment is found at the wrong address or unrecoverable in transit.
steps.work: Before any recovery step or credit, identify the source of the error, because that decides where the cost lands. Brick provided it, Brick absorbs the cost. The Network Operator provided or confirmed it, the cost passes back to the NO. The client provided it, the client absorbs it and Brick facilitates the resolution.
rules: Never start recovery or issue a credit before fault is determined.

steps.title: Escalate undetermined fault to a manager
steps.trigger: Fault cannot be clearly assigned to Brick, the NO or the client.
steps.work: Take the case to a manager for case-by-case resolution before any credit is issued. Recovery still proceeds in parallel.

steps.title: Attempt in-transit correction
steps.work: Contact the carrier immediately on discovering the error and try to redirect the package before it is delivered. This is the cheapest recovery and the only one available before delivery.

steps.title: Coordinate with the local Network Operator
steps.trigger: The package could not be redirected in transit.
steps.work: Have the local team physically check the address on file and any adjacent locations.

steps.title: Attempt a vendor return
steps.trigger: The package has been located after the event.
steps.work: Initiate a return to the vendor, for example Uline, for partial cost recovery.

steps.title: Document every recovery attempt
steps.work: Log who attempted recovery, the date and outcome of each attempt, and the final disposition of the package, in the relevant Work Order or client record in Portal. Skipping steps here can cost Brick unnecessarily.
rules: Every recovery step must be documented before any credit is offered.

steps.title: Was the package recovered?
steps.trigger: Recovery steps are exhausted and documented.
steps.work: A recovered package returned to the vendor needs no credit at all. A lost package moves to the resolution framework.

steps.title: Restock or reorder, no credit
steps.trigger: The package was recovered and returned to the vendor.
steps.work: No credit is needed regardless of fault. Restock or reorder the items and close the case.

steps.title: Apply the resolution framework
steps.trigger: The package is lost and recovery is exhausted.
steps.work: Route by fault. A credit reflects item cost only unless event execution was demonstrably impacted, in which case goodwill may apply on top. If execution was not impacted, a straight cost credit is the standard resolution and needs no extra escalation.

next.label: Brick at fault: credit the client
NO at fault: recover from the NO

steps.title: Client absorbs the cost
steps.trigger: The client provided the incorrect address.
steps.work: The client absorbs the cost. Brick facilitates the resolution and documents the outcome in writing.

steps.title: Escalate for goodwill credit
steps.work: Escalate. An additional goodwill credit beyond item cost may apply, which is a judgement call rather than the standard framework.

steps.title: Get the credit approved at the right threshold
steps.owner: Team lead, manager, or senior leadership by amount
steps.trigger: A credit to the client has been decided.
steps.work: Approval depends on the amount: under $100 a team lead or account owner may approve independently; $100 to $250 needs secondary stakeholder sign-off from a manager or ops lead; over $250 must be escalated to senior leadership before issuance.

steps.title: Get secondary stakeholder sign-off
steps.work: A manager or ops lead signs off before the credit is issued.

steps.title: Escalate to senior leadership
steps.work: Senior leadership must approve before the credit is issued.
rules: Credits over $250 are never issued without senior leadership approval.

steps.title: Issue the credit and confirm it in writing
steps.trigger: The credit is approved at its threshold.
steps.work: Issue the credit for item cost, and document and communicate it to the client in writing by email or a Portal note.
rules: Every client credit is documented and communicated in writing.

steps.title: Recover the cost from the Network Operator
steps.trigger: The NO provided or confirmed the incorrect address.
steps.work: Deduct the item cost from the NO's next payout, or flag it on the next invoice with a written explanation. Notify the NO in writing with the date, event, items affected and the amount to be deducted.
rules: The NO is always notified in writing before a deduction lands.
